comparison_policy: Never pool raw scores across benchmarks with different task sets, models, harnesses, judges, metrics or execution environments.
Store the observation date, model/harness context, task denominator, uncertainty interval and live-versus-historical page state for every result.
Treat browser-tool benchmarks as tool-operation evidence, not frontend code-generation evidence.
Reproduce native task splits and scorers before making superiority claims; preserve failed, blocked and unparseable runs in denominators.

comparators.name: Vision2Web
comparators.scope: Visual website development across static responsive pages, interactive multi-page frontends and full-stack applications; GUI workflow verification plus VLM visual judging.

observations.display: No results yet for this season

limitations: The 82.3 row is a historical snapshot, not a verified current-season leader.
Visual and functional level components are not directly comparable to SFEB's internal scorecard.
Official evaluation uses its own task set, submission format and current-season VLM/GUI judge.

comparators.name: Design2Code
comparators.scope: Screenshot-conditioned frontend reconstruction of real-world webpages, with automatic rendering metrics and human evaluation.

observations.metrics: automatic rendering metrics validated with human evaluation

limitations: Primarily measures screenshot-to-code visual reconstruction, not the complete functional, security, causal repair or maintenance loop.
Fixture and asset reuse requires a separate license and provenance review.

comparators.name: WebdriverIO Browser Agent Benchmark
comparators.scope: Browser-tool comparison: same model, harness and prompt while swapping browser tools; live website tasks judged by WebJudge.

observations.model_context: page lists two model contexts; the indexed aggregate row is not a model-independent result

limitations: The benchmark page's indexed October data shows published rows, while a direct page render on 2026-11-22 displayed an empty run-log state; retain this as an October historical snapshot, not a live leaderboard claim.
The 62% row aggregates 165 task observations; it must not be described as a clean 62/100 single-run result.
The benchmark reports roughly ±10 percentage-point intervals for 100 tasks and warns that overlapping intervals are not reliable rankings.
Live sites, bot blocks and CAPTCHAs reduce repeatability; WebJudge disagrees with human reviewers on about one run in seven.
This measures browser-tool effectiveness, not generated frontend quality.

comparators.name: SWE-Bench Pro task-quality audit
comparators.scope: Meta-evaluation of benchmark task validity: strictness, underspecification, test coverage and prompt correctness.
limitations: This is a task-quality audit, not an agent performance leaderboard.
The reported problem fraction applies to the audited SWE-Bench Pro public split, not to SFEB or Vision2Web.
